summary.name: Monitoring without Infrastructure @ Airbnb
summary.one_liner: A 2015 SREcon15 conference talk by Airbnb engineer Igor Serebryany on how Airbnb monitored its systems using open-source software, third-party vendors, and a configuration-as-code alerting framework.
keywords: monitoring tens of thousands of metrics
billions of log lines per day
use_cases: Monitoring a large fleet of machines with a small operations team
Aggregating and analyzing billions of log lines per day
Collecting and alerting on tens of thousands of metrics
Defining alerts as code in version-controlled configuration
Learning how a large company combined open-source and vendor monitoring tools
summary.what_it_does: The page is the abstract and speaker bio for a talk at SREcon15 (Santa Clara, March 2015). The talk describes how Airbnb built monitoring for its traffic-heavy systems without an in-house monitoring system, combining open-source software, third-party vendors, and custom glue code. Tools named are logstash, statsd, NewRelic, and Datadog. It also covers Airbnb's own open-sourced configuration-as-code alerting framework. The speaker says the setup manages tens of thousands of metrics and billions of log lines per day from thousands of machines, operated by less than one full-time engineer.
